73.79184,18.55846.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. Operated by Novosalus. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-92.28963,34.74651.name: Arkansas Children's Research Institute
-92.28963,34.74651.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-51.17964,-29.16850.name: Conception Centro de ReproduÃ§Ã£o Humana
-51.17964,-29.16850.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: https://www.conceptionbr.com/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

-83.37783,33.94487.name: University of Georgia
-83.37783,33.94487.state: 1197 S Lumpkin St, Athens, GA 30602, United States, United States
-83.37783,33.94487.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Georgia University. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on human health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

121.61000,31.21000.name: WuXi AppTec
121.61000,31.21000.desc: One of the largest contract research and manufacturing organisations in the world, China-based, working for a substantial share of the global pharmaceutical industry. US legislative attempts to restrict it revealed how central it had become: many Western drugs, including biologics, depend on it somewhere in the chain, and the companies opposing restriction were its clients.

-122.29600,37.88300.name: Bio-Rad Laboratories
-122.29600,37.88300.desc: A supplier of laboratory instruments and reagents, including droplet digital PCR used to detect and quantify engineered sequences in food and seed. Testing for unauthorised GM presence at low concentrations depends on this class of instrument, so the ability to find engineered material is itself a purchased product.

28.04730,-26.20410.name: African Centre for Biodiversity — corporate research
28.04730,-26.20410.desc: A South African organisation researching seed and agricultural corporations in Africa, publishing on ownership, philanthropy and policy influence. Independent research on this industry from within Africa is scarce, and this is one of the few sustained sources.

28.04730,-26.20410.name: Legal Aid South Africa
28.04730,-26.20410.desc: The state-funded legal assistance body that represented the non-profit which took the drought-tolerant maize approval to the Supreme Court of Appeal and won. It is on this map because it answers the question every other case entry raises and none of them resolves: who pays for nine years of litigation against a multinational and a government department. Legal standing without funded representation is a right nobody can exercise, and in this instance a publicly funded service is what made the difference between a documented objection and a judgment that set the approval aside.
